## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 14 user-facing changes.
### Fixed
- Next Space and Previous Space slide around from the last Space to the first, and back, instead of jumping. - A Space switch keeps sliding when you show or hide the sidebar during it, instead of jumping to the end. - On macOS 26, switches, pickers and the house choices in Settings take every click instead of ignoring clicks after the first. - Restart and Update quits Crest and installs the update instead of waiting until you quit, and Quit in the Dock works again, even after another app has used AppleScript with Crest. - Crest quits instead of waiting indefinitely when a Space couldn’t be fully deleted, and tries deleting that Space again the next time it opens. - Chromium is updated to 155.0.8059.39 with upstream security and compatibility fixes. - Opening an http:// address that can’t be reached shows Crest’s error page instead of closing Crest. - A link route set to “Is Exactly” with just a site’s name, such as docs.google.com, now matches that site’s home page, and Links settings say that routes apply to links from other apps. - A link route’s address field takes clicks and typing, with “example.com” shown as a hint inside it instead of a fixed label beside it. - In a narrow window, a Space’s Crest Studio no longer covers the Settings sidebar, so its search field and Space buttons take clicks again. - Typing a local address such as 192.168.0.1 or printer.local opens it over http, as other browsers do, and an address typed with http:// always opens over http. - When a page can’t be opened, its tab in the sidebar shows the site it tried to open instead of the previous page’s title.
---

## Highlights
### Fixed
- On pinned tabs, the sound and sharing badge sits in the tile’s bottom corner instead of over the site icon, so the icon is easy to click.
---
Stable releases are signed, notarized, and ready for everyday use.

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
